description: The default enforceable controls. They mirror the structural lints of the core in an exportable, firm-readable form, and they are the controls a firm inherits before it writes a single rule of its own. A control a firm must be able to defend to a regulator belongs here; a control that cannot be evaluated by code does not.

rules.description: An indicator claim must name the indicator it asserts. A pattern with no name is a pattern nobody can check, and a name that is not in the pack is a claim about a rule that does not exist.
rules.message: An indicator claim must name at least one indicator id from the declared knowledge pack.

rules.description: An adverse reading may not stand alone. Where an adverse reading is present, a benign reading must compete with it. This is the structural defence that a keyword filter cannot provide.
rules.message: An adverse reading is present with no benign reading to compete with it.

rules.description: A risk assessment must either cite evidence or state that the information is insufficient. An assessment that cites nothing and asserts a level is an assertion the artifact does not support.
rules.message: A risk assessment must cite evidence or be stated as insufficient_information.

rules.description: A recommendation must be anchored to evidence or to the claim that motivates it. A recommendation with neither is an instruction the artifact does not support.
rules.message: A recommendation must cite evidence or explain the claim that motivates it.

rules.description: Model-authored text may not assert that the subject is a criminal. The patterns are the same narrow set the core's culpability lint uses, and the check is negation-aware, so a statement that rules the conduct out is not a violation.
rules.message: The statement asserts criminality of the subject. The skill layer may not reach that conclusion.

rules.description: A conclusion drawn from an incomplete evidence set may not be stated with high confidence. The rule applies only to a partial evidence set, which is what the gate reads.
rules.message: The evidence set is partial, so a conclusion drawn from it may not be stated at high confidence.

procedural_policies.description: The evidence inventory is built before anything is asserted. A claim made before the analyst knows what evidence exists is a claim about a world the analyst has not seen.
procedural_policies.check: The artifact carries a non-empty evidence inventory, and it was built before the first claim was drafted.
procedural_policies.measured_by: The evaluation suite, through the stage order the artifact records.

notes: The enforceable rules here mirror the structural lints R-2, R-3b, R-4, R-8 and R-10 of the core. The lints remain the per-claim checks; this set is their exportable form, and it is what a firm reads when it has to explain a control to a regulator. A firm set overrides this set rule by rule, never wholesale.
